releases.body:
Recalled code changes keep library edits ahead of `*_test.py` files and leave
out scratch `*_test.py` files written outside a test directory.

### Fixed

- `FinalChanges` classifies `*_test.py` files alongside `test_*.py` as tests,
  so library edits appear before test edits in a recalled session's code changes
  and scratch `*_test.py` files outside a test directory are left out (#5751).

### Changed

- The README, architecture guide, roadmap and site lead with `codex`,
  `opencode`, `cursor` and `claude` on equal footing, and internal benchmark
  stands were removed from `scripts/` (#5751).
- The release follow-up workflow opens the manifest and extension version
  catch-up pull request automatically when `RELEASE_PIN_TOKEN` is set (#5749).

## Changelog
### Other
* chore: drop one-off measurement probes and local harness stands (#5751)
* chore: pin the manifests to 0.23.2 (#5746)
* ci: release follow-up opens the manifest pin PR itself (#5749)

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/main/install.sh | sh
go install github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/cmd/deja@v0.23.3
brew install deja-vu
```

releases.name: Nightly 2026-10-29
releases.body:
Built from d3d7a4cc on 2026-10-29.

Unreleased code — use a tagged release unless you are testing something specific.

Download with: gh release download nightly

Recall is twice as fast and the index a third smaller, with the same answers.
On a 19k-session store against 0.23.1, MCP recall p50 goes from 170 to 85 ms
and the index from 277 to 185 MB, and LongMemEval-S hit@1 is 88.9 against
88.1. Agents get less noise: the per-prompt block is injected for 51 unrelated
prompts in 240 instead of 171, and pages with nothing to find are a third of
their size. A recall that misses the deadline still reaches the agent, and
recall answers during an upgrade's rebuild. Cold builds cost 31% more CPU than
0.23.1 because the index now records the commands and edits behind each
conclusion. The index rebuilds once on upgrade.

### Added

- `deja mcp --context-search` serves Qwen Code's External Context MCP
  Profile v1: one `context_search({query})` tool that answers from the local
  index with at most five items in the profile's untrusted envelope, checked
  against the profile's published schemas and test vectors. `deja mcp` itself
  is unchanged. Register it with `qwen mcp add deja-context deja mcp
  --context-search --timeout 8000 --include-tools context_search` (#5662).
- `DEJA_RECALL_GLOBAL=1` makes MCP recall, `deja recall` and `deja mcp
  --context-search` rank every project the same instead of putting the current
  one first. Unset, nothing changes, and the hooks and the TUI keep their
  scope. From @Terminator637 (#5674).

### Changed

- Recall labels who wrote each line (`Model said (no record backs it)`,
  `Prompt written by a parent agent`, `Output with an instruction to agents` …)
  and shows the command or edit a model's conclusion rests on above the
  conclusion, from receipts written when the index is built or updated. A check or build
  rule a person typed in an interactive Claude Code session of the current
  project is shown as `User said (this project)`, and the frame header and MCP
  instructions say to follow those lines and nothing else. An instruction to
  run something that no person in the project typed (tool output, a paste, a
  parent agent's prompt, a `claude -p` run, another project) is cut to
  `[instruction to agents left out]`; a rule the person took back is not
  shown. The index version is now 109, so the store rebuilds once on the
  first run.
- Recall no longer heads a page "No session is about this" when a session on
  it holds most of a long query. The page says which session holds how many of
  the query's words and which it lacks. A page that shares only filler words
  with the query, or lacks the path or identifier it names, keeps the old line.
  A word-form match that had to drop query words no longer outranks the
  sessions that hold them.
- The instructions, skills and extensions ask for 1-3 exact terms on recall (a
  file path, an error string, a flag or identifier) instead of the task's key
  nouns. Queries of six or more words almost never matched.
- The instructions, skills and extensions no longer tell the agent that a
  recalled rule outranks its defaults. Recall is untrusted reference data from
  past transcripts: the agent names the rule in one line and asks before it
  changes a command, a file write or a config. The standing-decisions block
  says the same (#5676).
- The per-prompt line names the agent the memory came from and how long ago:
  `deja-vu — from Codex CLI, 4 months ago: "<quote>" (via <terms>)`, where it
  used to say only "you have been here" and a date. The gates are unchanged:
  a confident match only, at most once in twenty minutes per session. The dsh
  card and the OpenClaw chat line read both shapes (#5660).
- A spawned subagent's instructions are no longer extended with recall, except
  in Grok, whose main-thread hooks print to nobody. Over 60 days on one
  machine, 1339 Claude Code subagents were handed a block and none used it,
  and those blocks were 55% of all per-prompt recall. opencode task sessions
  are not searched on their turns either, since the agent that wrote them had
  the recall already (#5660).
- The per-promp

Big stores build and search for less. A cold build peaks at half the memory
it did (4.7 GB instead of 9.4 GB on 40,000 sessions, 2.4 GB instead of 4.0 GB
on a 12,000-session Codex store), redacts with 17x less CPU, reads each
transcript line once and writes a quarter of the scratch data. The slowest
searches answer in under 200 ms in process instead of up to 800, and a search
over many copies or look-alike sessions is no longer quadratic, a slowdown
0.23.0 made worse. MiniMax Code is the forty-third harness, a directory tree
can be named as one project in `~/.config/deja/projects`, and
`deja search --sort date` lists the newest match first. A friction wall that
was fixed leaves the session-start block. `deja secrets --scrub`
no longer breaks the transcripts it rewrites. The index is rebuilt once on
upgrade.

### Added

- MiniMax Code: sessions under `~/.minimax/v2/sessions` are indexed with the
  person's own words rather than the runtime's reminders, `deja resume` prints
  `mcode --session <id>`, and `deja install mcode` / `mcode-auto` write the MCP
  entry and a hook plugin. From @yangala (#5415, #5593).
- `~/.config/deja/projects` names a directory tree as one project, one
  `<path> = <name>` per line. Every checkout and worktree under a listed path
  is indexed under that name, and the hooks and recall standing anywhere in it
  scope to all of them. Editing the file renames nothing already indexed:
  `deja index` and `deja doctor` say a rebuild is due, `deja index --rebuild`
  renames the sessions whose transcripts are still on disk, and sessions
  indexed before the file existed still match from their own checkout until
  then. The exclude file wins over an alias, so a repository excluded by its
  own name stays out. From @Maweill (#5097, #5373).
- `deja search --sort date` lists the newest match first, in the text and in
  `--json`, and `^s` in the search screen turns the list newest first under
  day headings and back. On a common word the page is the newest of the whole
  match, not the newest of the best-ranked thousand (#5577, #5587).
- Guides for deleting Antigravity and Junie history. From @notsubash (#5604)
  and @Kasa-Harendra (#5624).
- A friction wall whose cause was fixed no longer stays in the session-start
  block for good. It drops out after 30 days without a hit while its projects
  keep getting new sessions, and `deja friction --settle <id>` takes it out at
  once, using the id each row of `deja friction` now prints. A session started
  after the settle that hits it again brings it back; `--unsettle` undoes it.
  Reported by @SmoothSailingMusic (#5628, #5631).

### Changed

- A cold build reads each transcript line once instead of handing it to six
  readers that each decoded it again, and checks tool output for known errors
  in one pass per line: 60 s instead of 87 s and 353 CPU-seconds instead of
  551 on 40,000 sessions (#5586). It also keys messages without allocating a
  string per word, which halves the indexing phase: 9.3 s to 4.2 s on a
  12,000-session Codex store, and the whole build from 273 to 215
  CPU-seconds (#5567).
- A cold build peaks at half the memory: 4.7 GB instead of 9.4 GB on a
  40,000-session store. The message count and the rebuild's dedupe set key on
  a hash instead of the text, and a full build runs the collector at GOGC=25
  unless GOGC or GOMEMLIMIT is set (#5498). A store under 20,000 sessions no
  longer holds every session's words at once to count which words go
  together: a 12,000-session Codex store peaks at 2.4 GB instead of 4.0 GB
  (#5533).
- Redacting secrets during a build takes 17x less CPU with the same output: on
  a 12,000-session Codex store the cold build went from 109 s to 45 s wall and
  904 s to 285 s of CPU (#5512).
- A cold build derives each session's row on every core instead of in the
  write loop: 189-202 s to 157-169 s on a 40,000-session store (#5524).
- A cold build writes a quarter of the scratch data it did, so a busy disk
  no longer stalls

Big stores are cheap to keep up to date. A pass that replaces a few sessions
appends their records instead of writing the whole log again and reads only
what changed: on a 40,000-session store 20 rewritten transcripts take 1.7 s
instead of 24 s, and peak memory drops from 7 GB to under 1 GB. A search for a
word most sessions hold answers in about a second instead of 24. Text taken
out of a transcript leaves the index on the next pass. For busy machines there
are `DEJA_NO_AUTO_INDEX` and `DEJA_SEARCH_ONLY`, and `deja index` exits 3 on a
partial run. Sub-agents are sessions of their own in every reader that marks
one, forks no longer take credit for what they copied, and recalled history
can no longer run a command in opencode or end a dsh turn. The index is rebuilt
once on upgrade.

A search for a word most sessions hold no longer reads all of them to show a page. Past 1,000 matches it ranks them first from the postings and the manifest, then reads the 1,000 that can reach the page and 200 more that check its length estimate; the total still counts every match, and `--all` scores every one as before. On a 40,000-session store a word in every session takes 1.1 s and 370 MB instead of 24 s and 2.6 GB, and MCP `recall` 2.5 s instead of 30 s (#5467).

The first index pass after a full build that rewrites, deletes or renames transcripts no longer reads the whole record log for the command-failure table: on a 40,000-session store, 20 rewritten transcripts take 4.0 s instead of 21 s, and the build leaves the table's state for that pass to start from (#5465). Renaming a transcript that shares its session with another file reads the session again only when the rename moves it past another of its files; 20 renames on the same store take 3.2 s instead of 20 s (#5466).
`deja --re` anchors `^` and `$` at each line, as grep does. They anchored the whole message, so `^panic:` missed a panic printed after any other tool output (#5448).
`deja embed` no longer sends a whole Cursor, Continue or Cline session again each time it grows. Those harnesses date unstamped turns from the file's modification time, and the vector identity held the time; it now holds only the session, role and text, so a session grown by one exchange embeds 2 records instead of every one. A version 2 sidecar is rekeyed on the next run without embedding again (#4976).

A search excerpt keeps the line that matched when it looks like tool noise. Searching `assignment to entry in nil map` showed the stack frames of a Go test panic and dropped the `panic:` line itself; `panic:`, `goroutine N`, `npm ERR!` and numbered lines are still left out when they do not hold the match (#5456). A `--re` search that finds nothing suggests a looser pattern, dropping `^`/`$`, or plain words, instead of "try fewer words or --re" (#5457).

`deja sync import` also leaves out a peer's records for a store `DEJA_EXCLUDE_HARNESSES` (or a `harness:` line) excludes and for a project the policy `ignore` rule covers, and says how many; a relay no longer sends an excluded store's sessions on (#5435). The `sync-timer` unit carries the `DEJA_*` and `XDG_*` settings of the shell it was installed from, so a timer run syncs into the same index under the same switches (#5436).

A dsh turn no longer fails when recalled history contains `{{...}}`. dsh read deja's project digest and recall as prompt templates, so a past session quoting `{{cwd}}` ended every new turn with `unknown prompt variable` before the model was called; both contexts now pass `interpolate: false` and split the braces (`{ {cwd} }`), which dsh before 0.2.1-alpha.2 needs, in the npm plugin and in `deja install dsh-auto` (#5421).
`deja sync` holds a peer's records to this machine's switches: `DEJA_INDEX_TOOL_OUTPUT=0`, `DEJA_INDEX_COMMANDS=0`, `DEJA_INDEX_PATHS=0`, `DEJA_INDEX_EDITS=0`, `DEJA_INDEX_WRITES=0` and `DEJA_INCLUDE_SUBAGENTS=0` leave the same records out of an import as out of a local read, and the import says how many (#5425).
Recalled

issues.title: CJK bigrams cost 17.5% of full-build time
edit spans: nineteen readers still record the path without the change line-level blame needs
The agent can reach 6 of deja's 40 commands, and those 6 cost 1915 tokens a session
the pre-tool hook costs 172 ms a call and returns a decision 0 times in 48 on a real store
three quarters of injected blocks carry a mention rather than a conclusion
Semantic tier: key vectors by content so they survive index rewrites, and let vectors retrieve on their own
